failure_summary.description: Agents favored salient contextual matches or narrower alternatives over the clue’s exact target, wording, and requested scope, despite existing guidance to resolve the whole clue.
The agent identified Clark but gave the full name Wesley Clark instead of the supported, unambiguous surname.
The clue required undoing a Spoonerism to recover the intended phrase, a transformation not explicitly covered by the current wordplay guidance.

patch.reasoning: Most failures disregard existing target, scope, or evidence rules, so repeating those rules would not address a skill gap. Add only the missing operational guidance for clues asking what a Spoonerism meant.

edits.content: When a clue asks what a Spoonerism or similar sound-transposition was intended to say, reverse the swapped sounds to recover the intended words and answer with that phrase, not the garbled wording. If the clue instead asks for the Spoonerism itself, give the transposed phrase.
